exposure: Body Mass Index (BMI) change during pregnancy
Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs Vaginal birth)
Body Mass Index (BMI) increase >5.7 during pregnancy
outcome: Zonulin concentrations in maternal serum, stool, umbilical cord serum, newborn meconium, and newborn stool at age seven days
Calprotectin concentrations in maternal stool, newborn meconium, and newborn stool at age seven days
cohort: 100 healthy, full-term newborns breastfed in the first week of life, and their mothers
finding: Maternal-foetal factors such as caesarean section, antibiotic therapy during pregnancy, and changes in the mother's BMI during pregnancy may increase intestinal permeability in newborns.
mod_finding: Newborns born via caesarean section had higher zonulin concentrations in their stool at seven days compared to those born vaginally.
